title: One neighbourhood locator and a large dimensioned constraints close-up (dimension lines on the edges they measure, each naming its basis; street names with mapped widths; north arrow and scale), a compact heights table and the 'No building placed' legend entry
objective: Page 2 keeps the neighbourhood locator only (the block close-up is not printed; block_map.py and its tests stay, restorable). Page 3 becomes a large close frame: the subject lot and the lots sharing an edge with it (1, 11, 61) dominate; dimension lines anchored to the outline's edges on the only basis the 1.4.0 document has (the city map outline, gis), each labelled in plain words (e.g. '103.88 ft, map outline, not surveyed'); street names with mapped widths (Northern Boulevard 100 ft, 215 Place 60 ft), north arrow and scale bar. The page-1 graphic becomes the compact close frame (maps side only). The six height rows become a compact 3x2 standard / qualifying-housing table. The site page shows the 'No building placed' legend entry instead of the sentence. No tax-map value is drawn. The rows' 'Not known' data path (page_site_context.py:52) stays for a later task. No CSS change: every SVG is sized from its viewBox; any page-2/3 CSS need goes to the orchestrator, who relays it to the M5-T165 builder. NB-04 revision 2 adds close_frame_dimensions.py to its code_paths and every drawn edge value not yet recorded (at least 99.98 and 101.71 ft) as gis quantities; its research_status stays unchanged.
business_reason: D-094 R014/R074: the maps repeat context while the property stays small; the constraints page needs a close-up drawing with dimensions attached to the boundaries.

acceptance_scenarios.then: every dimension endpoint lies on its edge's vertices within 0.01 ft; the drawing states its basis once in a note under it and each label shows only the figure (a label carries a short basis tag only when one drawing mixes bases; owner K1, D-094-R116); nothing is merged across bases; no tax-map value is drawn
